tasks.title: Remove dispatcher.wait() from Tk event-loop thread
tasks.end_goal: Every operation that touches disk, git, or the network is submitted non-blocking to the dispatcher worker pool and the Tk thread returns immediately. The user can scroll the tree, resize panes, and navigate the editor while a snapshot compile or git push is running. The existing gui_queue → process_gui_queue channel is the sole path for results, errors, progress events, and approval dialogs to reach the UI. No modal blocking of the event loop for any I/O operation.
tasks.current_state: action() → perform() → dispatcher.wait(operation, None) is called synchronously on the Tk thread. The worker runs on a ThreadPoolExecutor, but the Tk callback blocks inside dispatcher.wait() until the worker finishes. Result: every disk, snapshot, git, export, patch, and backup operation freezes the entire UI for its full duration despite the worker-thread infrastructure already being in place.
tasks.target_state: A new action_async(name, payload, on_success=None, on_error=None) method submits work to dispatcher and returns to Tk immediately. on_success/on_error callbacks are posted via gui_queue. The existing approval dialog flow (currently a blocking mid-operation wait) is restructured: the worker posts an approval request to gui_queue, Tk shows the dialog, the user's choice is posted back to the worker thread via a threading.Event or queue. Synchronous action() is retained unchanged for sub-millisecond state queries and all CLI/test callers — no test changes required for the initial migration.
